# Results — Study 750 (Return-to-Office)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim — **when a marquee
employer orders workers back to the office, beaten-down office landlords should pop** —
tested as a textbook short-window **event study on a sector basket**: around each dated
RTO-mandate announcement, the **cumulative abnormal return** (CAR) of an equal-weight
office-REIT basket is the basket's return minus a **market-model** fit (`basket = α + β·SPY`)
estimated on a clean pre-event window, cumulated over the event window. Events come from a
**hardcoded, cited table** of ~26 real RTO mandates (full 5-day "strict" vs "hybrid").
Offline core + synthetic control are deterministic; run `python examples/verify.py` to
reproduce every number.*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily adjusted closes — 10 office REITs + SPY + VNQ (public, no key) |
| Office basket | equal-weight `SLG, BXP, VNO, KRC, HIW, DEI, CUZ, HPP, BDN, ESRT` |
| Event table | hardcoded `RTO_EVENTS` (date, employer, strict/hybrid), fingerprint **69ca30fe1b8b** |
| As-of | 2026-07-10 |
| Events in table | **26** dated mandates (2021-02-25 → 2025-02-27); all **26** priced |
| Buckets | **18 strict** (full 5-day) / **8 hybrid** (2–4 day) |
| Benchmark / model | market model `basket = α + β·SPY`, 120-day estimation window, 10-day gap |
| Event window | CAR **[0, +2]** trading days (canonical); robustness over [0,0], [−1,+1], [0,+4] |
| Entry / costs | tradable variant enters **1 day after** the announcement; one-way 10-bps round-trip |
| Context proxy | Kastle 10-city office occupancy (Feb-2020=100) — **labelled, cited, not priced** |

> **Survivorship, named on the Signal axis.** The basket is the office landlords that
> *survived* the WFH shock. The worst casualties left the tape entirely — **WeWork** went
> bankrupt and delisted (Nov 2023), hundreds of private towers were handed to lenders via
> **CMBS default**, and distressed names (OPI) reverse-split out of relevance. So the priced
> basket is biased **against** the very distress the RTO story is supposed to reverse; for a
> short-window *reaction* study that mostly pulls the estimate **toward zero**, making a
> survivor basket that fails to pop a **conservative** read of "RTO rescued the office."

## The signal — basket abnormal return around the mandate (canonical CAR[0,+2])

| bucket | n | mean CAR | win-rate (CAR>0) | *t* vs 0 |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **strict** (full 5-day RTO) | 18 | **−0.34%** | 44% | **−0.49** |
| **hybrid** (2–4 day) | 8 | −0.43% | 50% | −0.52 |
| all events | 26 | **−0.37%** | 46% | **−0.69** |

**strict − hybrid = +0.09pp**, Welch ***t* = +0.08**; all-events **placebo *p* = 0.53**
(share of random same-size basket windows whose mean CAR matches/beats the mandate set;
null mean ≈ 0.00%). Read it plainly: the office-REIT basket's average reaction to a big
employer's RTO mandate is a **statistically-zero −0.37%** — if anything a faint *negative*
drift, the opposite of the believers' pop — and a *stricter* mandate does **not** move
offices more than a hybrid one (the gap is essentially zero, *t* = 0.08). The reaction sits
squarely inside the luck cloud.

## Robustness — no window, no benchmark rescues it

| event window | all-events mean | *t* | strict − hybrid | diff *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| [0, 0] | +0.23% | +0.69 | +0.50pp | +0.80 |
| **[0, +2]** (canonical) | −0.37% | −0.69 | +0.09pp | +0.08 |
| [−1, +1] | +0.30% | +0.50 | −0.52pp | −0.37 |
| [0, +4] | +0.14% | +0.18 | +1.90pp | +1.32 |

Every window's all-events CAR is a fraction of a percent with **|*t*| well under 1**, and
the strict−hybrid gap flips sign across windows (a hallmark of noise, not signal — it is
+0.50pp on the news day, −0.52pp over [−1,+1]). The widest window ([0,+4]) shows the
largest strict−hybrid gap (+1.90pp) but still only *t* = 1.32 — nowhere near the *t* ≥ 2 bar,
and window-shopped.

**Does office react *beyond* what all REITs did?** Swap the benchmark to the broad-REIT ETF
VNQ (so "abnormal" means *relative to the whole REIT complex*):

| window vs VNQ | all-events mean | *t* |
|---|--:|--:|
| [0, 0] | +0.21% | +0.85 |
| [0, +2] | +0.17% | +0.43 |

Still nothing. Office landlords do not move relative to the REIT sector on RTO news either —
consistent with offices being a **rates + secular-WFH** trade, not an announcement trade.

## The tradable version — enter the day after, and it's a small loss

| trade | all-events mean CAR | *t* | net @ 10 bps |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| enter **+1 day**, hold [+1,+3] | **−0.33%** | −0.47 | **−0.43%** |
| enter **+1 day**, hold [+1,+5] | −0.78% | −0.88 | −0.88% |

Apply a one-day execution lag — all you can do, since a mandate memo lands intraday and you
fill at the next close — and the basket's post-announcement CAR is a **small negative** of
either horizon, made worse by costs. There is no capturable pop to buy.

## Context proxy — desks did refill, and the REITs still didn't care (labelled proxy)

The Kastle Systems 10-city "Back to Work Barometer" (office badge swipes vs Feb-2020 = 100,
a **cited, approximate, hardcoded** series — *not* a priced tape) rose from **~24** in early
2021 to **~54** by early 2025 and then **plateaued near half**. So the physical
back-to-office trend is real but partial — and even that slow refill produced **no** repricing
of the office REITs on any single mandate. The desks came halfway back; the towers stayed a
macro story.

## Synthetic positive control — the engine is faithful, ~two dozen events are weak

A deterministic per-event abnormal-return panel (15 strict / 11 hybrid) with a **plantable
strict-bucket CAR edge**:

| planted strict edge | strict mean | strict *t* | hybrid mean | strict − hybrid *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **0 bps** (no edge) | +1.29% | +1.87 | +0.36% | **+1.01** |
| **+400 bps** (large) | +5.29% | +7.67 | +0.36% | **+5.35** |

With **no** planted edge the believers' actual object — the strict−hybrid gap — stays at
*t* = 1.01 (the noise nudges the single strict bucket to *t* = 1.87 but still short of 2, and
the *difference* that the claim rests on is comfortably null). Only an **implausibly large**
+4%/event planted edge drives the difference to *t* = 5.3. The control proves both things at
once: the engine recovers a real reaction when one exists, **and** a two-dozen-event calendar
is far too small to detect any RTO-reaction of plausible size on a sector that swings on rates.

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** The office-REIT basket's average CAR around an RTO mandate is
  **−0.37% at *t* = −0.69** (placebo *p* = 0.53), the strict−hybrid gap is **+0.09pp at
  *t* = 0.08**, and no window or benchmark (SPY or VNQ) clears |*t*| ~1. Not a faint edge —
  indistinguishable from zero, and if anything faintly *negative*, the wrong sign for a pop.
  **Survivorship** is named on this axis and points *toward* the null (the worst landlords
  delisted).
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** There is nothing to trade: the reaction is zero gross, the
  one-day-lag tradable variant is **−0.33%** (worse after 10 bps), and the sector's moves are
  a rates/secular-WFH story that a single memo doesn't budge. No edge, at any size.
- **Office rebound on RTO? — NOT SUPPORTED.** Desks physically refilled to ~half (Kastle
  proxy) and stalled, and the office REITs simply did not price the mandates. The romantic
  "RTO saves the office landlords" trade is a **narrative**, not a signal — the towers trade
  on rates and structural vacancy, not on who sent the back-to-work email.
